cards.front: Besides license suspension, what else can the nitrous oxide false-ID offense bring?
cards.back: Besides the license suspension, the nitrous oxide false-identification offense can also bring fines or a jail sentence.

cards.front: What are the risks of using nitrous oxide?
cards.back: Nitrous oxide, commonly called laughing gas, has legitimate uses such as an anesthetic for doctors and dentists, but it can be habit-forming, and using it over a long time can lead to serious health problems or death.

cards.front: How long is the suspension for a first nitrous oxide offense?
cards.back: A first nitrous oxide offense suspends your driving privilege for six months.

cards.front: How long is the suspension for a second or later nitrous oxide offense?
cards.back: A second or later nitrous oxide offense suspends your driving privilege for twelve months.

cards.front: How do first and repeat nitrous oxide suspensions differ?
cards.back: A first nitrous oxide offense means a six-month suspension, while a second or later one means twelve months.

cards.front: Is it lawful to display a license you know is suspended or altered?
cards.back: It is unlawful to display a license you know is canceled, revoked, suspended, fictitious or altered.

cards.front: What follows altering a license or getting a false one?
cards.back: Altering a license or obtaining a false driver license is illegal and leads to suspension, with possible fines or jail.

cards.front: Who may drive or be in physical control of a vehicle while under the influence?
cards.back: No one under the influence of alcohol, marijuana, medications or illegal drugs may drive or be in actual physical control of any vehicle.

cards.front: What is the Implied Consent Law?
cards.back: By applying for and accepting an Arizona driving privilege, you agree to be tested for alcohol and drugs if you are arrested for DUI, which is called the Implied Consent Law.

cards.front: What test may an officer ask for if you are suspected of DUI?
cards.back: An officer who has reason to believe you drove under the influence will ask you to take a blood, breath, urine or other bodily substance test.

cards.front: At what alcohol concentration do you lose your driving privilege on the spot?
cards.back: If a test shows an alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent or more, you lose your driving privilege on the spot.

cards.front: What is the on-the-spot limit when driving a vehicle that needs a commercial license?
cards.back: For someone driving a commercial vehicle that requires a commercial driver license, the on-the-spot limit is zero point zero four.

cards.front: For a driver under twenty-one, what alcohol concentration can bring suspension?
cards.back: A driver under twenty-one may have the license suspended for any alcohol concentration at all.

cards.front: How do the on-the-spot limits differ for ordinary, commercial and under-twenty-one drivers?
cards.back: The on-the-spot loss of privilege starts at zero point zero eight for an ordinary driver but at zero point zero four in a commercial vehicle that needs a commercial license, and any alcohol concentration can suspend a driver under twenty-one.
cards.memory_hook: point zero eight, zero four, any

cards.front: Can you be found guilty of driving while intoxicated below zero point zero eight?
cards.back: You may be found guilty of driving while intoxicated even when your BAC was below zero point zero eight percent.

cards.front: Is a BAC under zero point zero eight a defense?
cards.back: A BAC under zero point zero eight is not a defense, because a driver can still be found guilty of driving while intoxicated.

cards.front: What does refusing the tests after a DUI arrest cost you?
cards.back: Refusing or failing to complete the tests after a DUI arrest automatically costs you the privilege to drive: twelve months the first time, and twenty-four months if it is your second refusal in eighty-four months.

cards.front: How do first and second test refusals differ?
cards.back: A first test refusal costs twelve months of privilege, while a second refusal within eighty-four months costs twenty-four months.

cards.front: What happens to the privilege after a second or third DUI offense?
cards.back: For a second or third DUI offense, the driving privilege is automatically revoked in addition to any criminal penalties from the court.

cards.front: What is the minimum jail for a first DUI offense?
cards.back: A first DUI offense brings at least ten consecutive days in jail.

cards.front: What minimum suspension and fine does a first DUI bring?
cards.back: A first DUI offense brings a license suspension of at least ninety days and a fine of at least one thousand two hundred fifty dollars.

cards.front: Besides jail and fines, what does a first DUI require?
cards.back: A first DUI offense also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or evidence-based psychotherapy and community service, and the court may order an ignition interlock on any vehicle you drive.

cards.front: What minimum jail, fine and revocation does a second DUI bring?
cards.back: A second or later DUI offense brings at least ninety days in jail, a fine of at least three thousand dollars and a twelve-month license revocation.

cards.front: Besides jail, what does a second DUI require?
cards.back: A second or later DUI offense also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or psychotherapy and community service, and an ignition interlock may be ordered.

cards.front: How do the minimum penalties for a first and second DUI differ?
cards.back: A first DUI means at least ten consecutive days in jail and a ninety-day minimum suspension, while a second DUI means at least ninety days in jail and a twelve-month revocation.

cards.front: At what alcohol concentration does extreme DUI apply?
cards.back: Extreme DUI applies to a driver with an alcohol concentration of zero point one five or higher.

cards.front: What minimum jail and fine does a first extreme DUI bring?
cards.back: A first extreme DUI brings at least thirty consecutive days in jail and a fine of at least two thousand five hundred dollars.

cards.front: On a first extreme DUI at zero point two zero or higher, what is the minimum jail?
cards.back: On a first extreme DUI with an alcohol concentration of zero point two zero or higher, jail is at least forty-five days and a suspended sentence is not available.

cards.front: What device is required after a first extreme DUI?
cards.back: A first extreme DUI also requires alcohol screening, education or treatment or psychotherapy, community service, and a Certified Ignition Interlock Device on any vehicle you drive.

cards.front: What minimum fine and revocation does a repeat extreme DUI bring?
cards.back: A second or later extreme DUI brings a fine of at least three thousand two hundred fifty dollars and a twelve-month license revocation.

cards.front: On a repeat extreme DUI at zero point two zero or higher, what is the minimum jail?
cards.back: On a second or later extreme DUI at zero point two zero or higher, jail is at least one hundred eighty days with no suspended sentence.

cards.front: Besides jail and fines, what does a repeat extreme DUI require?
cards.back: A second or later extreme DUI also requires alcohol screening, education or treatment, an ignition interlock and community service.

cards.front: What are the two extreme DUI tiers?
cards.back: Extreme DUI begins at zero point one five, and a higher tier at zero point two zero raises the minimum jail to forty-five days on a first offense and one hundred eighty days on a repeat, with no suspended sentence.
cards.memory_hook: point one five, point two zero

cards.front: What are the four minimum DUI fines?
cards.back: Fines start at one thousand two hundred fifty dollars for a first DUI, two thousand five hundred dollars for a first extreme DUI, three thousand dollars for a second DUI and three thousand two hundred fifty dollars for a second extreme DUI.

cards.front: How do interlock rules differ for a first DUI and a first extreme DUI?
cards.back: For an ordinary first DUI the court may order an ignition interlock, while for a first extreme DUI the interlock is required.

cards.front: What three situations make a DUI aggravated?
cards.back: Aggravated DUI covers a DUI committed while your privilege is suspended or revoked, a third DUI in seven years, or a DUI with a person under fifteen in the vehicle.

cards.front: What kind of DUI is it when the driver is already required to use an interlock?
cards.back: Aggravated DUI also covers a DUI or extreme DUI by a person who is already required to use a Certified Ignition Interlock Device.

cards.front: What prison term and revocation does aggravated DUI bring?
cards.back: Aggravated DUI brings prison for not more than two years and a one-year license revocation, on top of any other required penalty.

cards.front: Besides prison, what does aggravated DUI require?
cards.back: Aggravated DUI also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or psychotherapy and an ignition interlock on any vehicle you drive.

cards.front: What do a third DUI in seven years and a child under fifteen aboard have in common?
cards.back: A third DUI within seven years and a DUI with a passenger under fifteen are both aggravated DUI, which carries prison for not more than two years.

cards.front: What is a Certified Ignition Interlock Device?
cards.back: A Certified Ignition Interlock Device is a breath alcohol tester wired into the vehicle's ignition and power system.

cards.front: When must the driver blow into an interlock first?
cards.back: The driver must blow into the interlock before trying to start the engine, and the vehicle will not start if the alcohol level is above a set level.

cards.front: When else must the driver blow into an interlock?
cards.back: While the vehicle is running, the driver must also blow into the interlock at random intervals.

cards.front: When does an interlock test the driver?
cards.back: An interlock test happens before starting the engine and again at random intervals while driving.

cards.front: When may a person apply for a Special Ignition Interlock Restricted Driver License?
cards.back: For most of the listed DUI-related cases, Arizona law lets a person apply for a Special Ignition Interlock Restricted Driver License on day one of a Class D or Class G suspension or revocation.

cards.front: What must an interlock restricted license holder do?
cards.back: A person holding an interlock restricted license must follow the interlock rules, finish any required alcohol treatment classes, and carry proof of future financial responsibility coverage.

cards.front: What does the Executive Hearing Office do?
cards.back: The Executive Hearing Office holds hearings requested by people or businesses contesting an MVD order.

cards.front: What are most Executive Hearing Office cases about?
cards.back: Most Executive Hearing Office cases are appeals of an order suspending or revoking a driver license, usually because of traffic law violations.

cards.front: What does the Executive Hearing Office hear most often?
cards.back: The Executive Hearing Office hears challenges to MVD orders, most often orders suspending or revoking a license.

recap_hooks.text: Nitrous oxide offenses bring six months, then twelve, and displaying or altering a bad license is illegal.
You lose your privilege on the spot at zero point zero eight, or zero point zero four in a commercial vehicle, and refusing a test costs twelve months.
A first DUI means at least ten days in jail and a ninety-day suspension; a second means at least ninety days in jail and revocation.
Extreme DUI starts at zero point one five, and a first extreme DUI requires an interlock.
A DUI while suspended, a third in seven years, or with a child under fifteen is aggravated, with up to two years in prison.
An interlock tests your breath before you start and at random while you drive.
